claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings protect zirconium-alloy cladding under low-temperature water conditions.
Elemental Cr coatings protect zirconium-alloy cladding under high-temperature steam conditions.
Elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 5 wt% Al to the Cr coating by co-deposition.
Al added to the Cr coating will segregate at the coating/substrate interface.
High-temperature exposure will cause the Al-containing coating to form a stable, self-limiting alumina-rich Cr-Al oxide layer.
During high-temperature steam exposure, Al will oxidize preferentially.
The alumina-rich oxide will act as a diffusion barrier between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
The proposed oxide barrier will reduce mutual diffusion of Cr and Zr.
Adding Al will maintain Cr-based oxidation protection under normal-water conditions.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr-Al coating will exhibit less Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr-Al coating will exhibit improved coating integrity.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr-Al coating will provide comparable or improved oxidation resistance in approximately 300°C subcritical water.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr-Al coating will provide comparable or improved oxidation resistance in approximately 1200°C steam.
The predicted normal-service performance boundary is approximately 300°C subcritical water for 1000 hours.
The predicted accident-performance boundary is approximately 1200°C steam for 2 minutes.
The predicted benefits are intended to hold in a radiation environment representative of nuclear service.
